From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: виня and Appendix:Variations of "vina"

Bulgarian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [viˈna]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -na

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vina. Synchronically, an old verbal noun from root Proto-Indo-European *weyh₁- (“to chase, to pursue”) + -на (-na). Cognate with Latvian vaina (“fault”).

Noun

[edit]

вина́ • (viná) f

  1. guilt, blame (property or emotion of being guilty)
    признавам/отричам вина ― priznavam/otričam vina ― to plead/not to plead guilty
    хвърлям вината върху някого ― hvǎrljam vinata vǎrhu njakogo ― to cast the blame on s.o.
  2. fault, responsibility (cause for some bad situation)
    по вина на някого ― po vina na njakogo ― through s.o. fault
    изкупувам нечия вина ― izkupuvam nečija vina ― to redeem s.o. fault
    нося вина за ― nosja vina za ― to bear responsibility for [something bad]

[edit]

verbs
  • виня́ (vinjá) (causative-iterative)
adjectives

  • вини́телен (vinítelen)
  • (dialectal) винова́т (vinovát)
  • вино́вен (vinóven)
  • неви́нен (nevínen)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

вина́ • (viná) n pl

  1. indefinite plural of ви́но (víno)
  2. indefinite plural of вино́ (vinó)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • нива (niva)

[edit]

Etymology

From Russian вино́ (vinó).

Noun

[edit]

вина • (vina)

  1. wine
  2. liquor

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian вино (vino). Akin to Udmurt вина (vina) and Komi-Permyak вина (vina).

Macedonian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈvina]
  • Hyphenation: ви‧на
  • Rhymes: -ina

Etymology 1

[edit]

    Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vina. Cognate with Russian вина (vina), Polish wina.

    Noun

    [edit]

    вина • (vina) f (plural вини, relational adjective виновен)

    1. guilt, fault
    Declension
    [edit]
    Declension of вина
    singular plural
    indefinite вина (vina) вини (vini)
    definite unspecified вината (vinata) вините (vinite)
    definite proximal винава (vinava) виниве (vinive)
    definite distal винана (vinana) винине (vinine)
    vocative вино (vino) вини (vini)

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

      See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

      Noun

      [edit]

      вина • (vina) pl

      1. inflection of вино n (vino, “wine”):
        1. indefinite plural
        2. vocative plural

      Old Church Slavonic

      [edit]

      Noun

      [edit]

      вина • (vina) f

      1. fault
      2. cause
      3. excuse

      Pannonian Rusyn

      [edit]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): [ˈvina]
      • Rhymes: -ina
      • Hyphenation: ви‧на

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      Inherited from Old Slovak vina, from Proto-Slavic *vina. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn вина́ (vyná) and Slovak vina.

      Noun

      [edit]

      вина (vina) f

      1. guilt, fault, blame, wrong
        Synonym: виноватосц (vinovatosc)

      Russian

      [edit]
      Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
      вина
      Wikipedia ru

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      Inherited from Old East Slavic вина (vina), from Proto-Slavic *vina; cognate with Latvian vaina.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): [vʲɪˈna]
      • Rhymes: -a

      Noun

      [edit]

      вина́ • (viná) f inan (genitive вины́, nominative plural ви́ны, genitive plural вин)

      1. guilt, fault; blame
        • 2011, Виктор Пелевин [Victor Pelevin], “Ч. 1. Damsel in distress, 10”, in S.N.U.F.F., Москва: Эксмо; English translation from Andrew Bromfield, transl., S.N.U.F.F., 2014:
          Всю остальну́ю доро́гу он молча́л, разду́мывая, как пра́вильно себя́ вести́ и что тако́го мо́жет показа́ть ему́ Хло́я, что́бы искупи́ть свою́ вину́ (верне́е, все свои́ многочи́сленные ви́ны).
          Vsju ostalʹnúju dorógu on molčál, razdúmyvaja, kak právilʹno sebjá vestí i što takóvo móžet pokazátʹ jemú Xlója, štóby iskupítʹ svojú vinú (vernéje, vse svoí mnogočíslennyje víny).
          He said nothing all the rest of the way, wondering how he ought to behave and what Chloe could possibly show him in order to atone for her sin (or rather, all her multitudinous sins).

      вина́ • (viná) n inan

      1. genitive singular of вино́ (vinó)
        • 1876, Russian Synodal Bible, Mark 2:22:
          Никто не вливает вина молодого в мехи ветхие: иначе молодое вино прорвет мехи, и вино вытечет, и мехи пропадут; но вино молодое надобно вливать в мехи новые.
          Nikto ne vlivajet vina molodovo v mexi vetxije: inače molodoje vino prorvet mexi, i vino vytečet, i mexi propadut; no vino molodoje nadobno vlivatʹ v mexi novyje.
